purpose: Edit delivered documents and perform governed headless report conversion.
linux_plan: Use the distribution package manager and its signed repository metadata.
Verify the executable version; defer document-conversion lifecycle proof until the dedicated proof session.
macos_plan: Use the conventional trusted package mechanism or The Document Foundation official distribution.
Verify the executable version; defer document-conversion lifecycle proof until the dedicated proof session.
windows_plan: Prefer the platform package manager and The Document Foundation package identity.
Only after a verified package-manager transport failure, resolve an installer through the official Metalink response.
Require the selected URL to be listed by that Metalink and require the published SHA-256 to match before execution.
Defer install, uninstall, reinstall, registration, headless-conversion, and cleanup proof to the dedicated Windows lifecycle session.

purpose: Inspect and prepare GIS desktop work that is not owned by the DS map surface.
provenance: QGIS project official distribution or the platform's trusted repository
linux_plan: Use the distribution package manager or the QGIS project's documented repository after an explicit install request.
macos_plan: Use the conventional trusted package mechanism or the QGIS project's official distribution after an explicit install request.
windows_plan: Use the platform package manager or the QGIS project's official installer after an explicit install request.

purpose: Provide the Git for Windows Bash environment when a Windows workflow explicitly needs it.
provenance: Git for Windows official distribution or the platform's trusted package catalog
linux_plan: Use the native Bash or selected login shell; Git Bash is a Windows product and is not emulated here.
macos_plan: Use the native shell and conventional package manager; Git Bash is a Windows product and is not emulated here.
windows_plan: Detect a suitable existing Git for Windows Bash first and leave it untouched when present.
Only an explicit future install request may authorize acquisition when it is absent.
